quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind gusts, blind spots, and surface hazards. Your position tells other drivers not to share your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: To help drivers merge safely from an entrance ramp into your lane, you should:

options.text: Move to another lane if you can.
Not worry about it—they are merging, not you.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to merge safely by moving to a different lane if you can.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about how many alcoholic drinks per hour?
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour on average. The time it takes to lower your blood alcohol level varies. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When your left arm is stretched straight out to the left, it means you plan to turn left or move left.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: The person who sold you the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual first for accurate information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if needed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Signs showing rules like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which formation keeps group riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when turning or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Use half their normal space cushions.
Keep enough space cushions around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space cushions around each rider.
questions.explanation: In a group, stay close but keep an adequate space cushion around your motorcycle.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay seated and lift your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep the motorcycle straight up and down. Just before impact, roll off the throttle a little to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It helps protect your whole face.
It works less well than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When do most crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips. They occur within the first five miles or just a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: What are the four steps to safely complete a turn?
questions.explanation: To safely turn, slow down, look through the turn to where you want to go, press the handlebar in the direction of the turn to lean the bike, and roll on the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you need to stop quickly, use both brakes. This habit makes quick stops easier.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a rider?
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: When you need to stop quickly, use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled by your right foot.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do to make a quick stop on wet pavement?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on slippery surfaces. Apply the front brake gradually to prevent the wheel from locking.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake and the skid will stop.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it again quickly.
Release the front brake immediately and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake right away. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: When the road is wet, which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane

questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in a strip down the center of each lane. This strip is slippery when wet. You can usually ride on either side of this strip and still stay in your lane.

questions.question: When should you keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When stopping will be harder than normal
When you want to see the scenery
To make other drivers cut you off
To hide your motorcycle from the driver ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than normal
questions.explanation: Keep extra space when your motorcycle will need more time to stop. This includes wet roads, poor visibility, or heavy traffic where a driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handlebar. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn
Keep your knees away from the gas tank
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you want to go

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you want to go
questions.explanation: Look through the turn by moving only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Every time you slow down or stop
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop your motorcycle.
